title: Smart Motorways & Emergency Areas
whatItIs: Smart motorways use variable speed limits and may use the hard shoulder as a lane. Some have no hard shoulder at all.
keyFacts: On some smart motorways there is no hard shoulder: in an emergency, go to an emergency area.
Emergency areas have an orange surface and a blue sign with an orange SOS phone.
A hard shoulder has a solid white line. Use it as a lane only when a speed limit shows above it.

keyFacts.text: Never drive in a lane closed by a red X.

keyFacts: If you stop in a live lane, put hazard lights on, stay belted in and call 999 if you can't get out safely.

items.title: Emergency areas
items.text: Orange surface, blue sign with an orange SOS phone. Use one if you have a problem.

items.title: Solid white line
items.text: A hard shoulder. Use it only when a speed limit shows above it.

items.title: Variable speed limits
items.text: Speeds shown in a red ring over the lanes are the law.

items.title: Stuck in a live lane
items.text: Hazard lights on, seat belt on, call 999 if it isn't safe to get out.

a.label: Solid white line
points: Use it only if a limit shows above it

b.label: Broken white line
points: Use it like any other lane

onTheTest.question: You break down on a smart motorway with no hard shoulder. Where should you try to stop?
onTheTest.why: Try to reach an emergency area or leave at the next exit. If you can't, move as far left as you can and put your hazard lights on.

traps: No speed limit over the hard shoulder means it isn't open as a lane.
Emergency areas are for emergencies, not for a rest.
Stuck in a live lane and can't get out safely? Stay belted in and call 999.
